rethink: The findings favour selling the owner's own licensed flying to Phoenix buyers who already pay for drone work, over generic marketplace gigs: Zeitview claim rates are 20-50% with about 40% weather cancellations (F5, F7), and ARMLS stays free only until January 2027 (F75). The held four directions all sit on one buyer or deliverable, so these routes use different buyers (photographers who lack a drone licence, construction firms) and pay at delivery, which avoids the net-30 and Prompt Payment Act lags (F31, F39, F40).

routes.title: White-label drone add-on for Phoenix real estate photographers
routes.payer: Independent Phoenix-area real estate photographers and small media companies that sell drone add-ons but lack a Part 107 pilot or a drone
routes.offer: Owner flies licensed exterior aerial photo and video for the photographer's listing shoot and hands over edited files under the photographer's brand, paid per job on delivery
routes.priceAnchor: Photographers sell drone add-ons at $100-300 (F29, F85) and packages with 2 drone angles from $249 (F80); a wholesale price of about $100 leaves them a margin. The wholesale price is my estimate.
routes.channel: Direct outreach to the 59 Arizona photographers listed on PropPhoto and to local MLS-listed photographers (F67, F103), plus a free PropPhoto listing (F74). Each job is a small one-off payment, so the first cash comes within the first week or two.
routes.fulfiller: The owner, flying the Mavic 3 under Part 107, with $1M liability insurance at about $62 a month (F22) as real estate clients require (F25)
routes.volumeBasis: The 59 photographers PropPhoto lists in Arizona (F67); the share that are Phoenix-area and lack a drone pilot has not been counted
routes.assumptions: Photographers pay on delivery or within days. Wholesale demand at about $100 exists. About 45 jobs in 60 days (roughly 5 photographers at 1-2 jobs a week) is reachable. The October closed-sales drop of 9.8% (F28) does not cut volume too far.
routes.ownerFit: Uses the Mavic 3, the Part 107 licence, the Phoenix location and the owner's own flying hours (about 80 of the 170 available in the window). Selling licensed flying to the buyers who pay for it.

routes.title: Construction progress aerial documentation for Phoenix builders
routes.payer: General contractors, homebuilders and developers with active sites in the Phoenix metro area
routes.offer: A flight of one active site, with an orthomosaic overview, dated progress photos and a short video, as a visual progress record. It is not a survey and makes no measurement or legal claim. Delivered within a day and billed on delivery, with a prepay option.
routes.priceAnchor: Zeitview construction progress mapping missions carry pilot pay of $300-500 for about 75 minutes (F26). Direct to the builder, $400 is in that range. The direct-to-builder price is my estimate.
routes.channel: Direct email and phone outreach to Phoenix-area builders, developers and site managers, built from permit and project lists. A one-flight trial gets a fast first sale. Paying on delivery avoids the contractor payment cycle in F39 and F40.
routes.fulfiller: The owner flies the Mavic 3 and processes the data with Pix4D or DroneDeploy. Both have free trials of 14-15 days (F10, F11), then an estimated $350 a month, with insurance at about $62 a month (F22).
routes.volumeBasis: My estimate, to be built from the active commercial and residential permits in Maricopa County; Arizona construction volume of $31.1B (F34) shows the market exists but gives no count of buyers
routes.assumptions: Builders will pay about $400 per flight at delivery. Contract terms stay inside 60 days. Calling it a progress record and not a survey stays clear of A.R.S. 32-101 and 32-145 (F12-F14, F59). Free trials plus one paid month cover the processing software.
routes.ownerFit: Uses the Mavic 3, the Part 107 licence, the Phoenix location and the owner's flying and processing hours (about 5 hours a job, F37)

routes.title: Drone pilot network missions as a stopgap
routes.payer: Zeitview, FlyGuys, Droners.io and The Droning Company clients who post missions in the Phoenix area
routes.offer: Owner claims and flies real estate marketing missions of about 30 minutes, or construction missions of about 75 minutes, at the fixed pay shown before accepting
routes.priceAnchor: Zeitview real estate marketing missions pay $125-225 (F72, F88) and construction missions $300-500 (F26). Pay is fixed before acceptance (F78).
routes.channel: Sign up with the networks named in F64 and use the push notifications for nearby missions (F68). No ad spend. Because of the weak claim rates in F7, this fills spare hours and does not carry the target.
routes.fulfiller: The owner flies the Mavic 3 with insurance at about $62 a month (F22). Network fees are 10% at Droners.io (F69) and $10 a month at The Droning Company (F70).
routes.volumeBasis: The four networks named in F64; mission counts in Phoenix are not published
routes.assumptions: Enough missions are posted near Phoenix and the owner wins a few. Settlement comes within about 14 days of acceptance (F76 for FlyGuys; others unchecked). Weather cancels about 40% of missions (F5).
